Case_19009/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Frontal chest XR showed prominent opacity in the right paratracheal region

description.short_caption: Frontal chest radiograph showing prominent opacity in the right paratracheal region.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating a prominent opacity in the right paratracheal region. The opacity appears well-defined and is located adjacent to the trachea, suggestive of a mediastinal or paratracheal abnormality. The lung fields are otherwise clear, and the cardiac silhouette is within normal limits. No obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible.
visible_findings: prominent opacity in the right paratracheal region

Case_19009/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: a) Axial CT chest revealed a 4 cm focal consolidative process in the medial right upper lobe with large central area of necrosis and early cavitation; b) Coronal CT chest revealed focal necrotizing consolidation with cavitation that extends from the right lung apex to the anterior of the right hilar region

description.short_caption: Axial and coronal CT images showing necrotizing consolidation with cavitation in the right upper lobe.
description.detailed_description: This image consists of two CT chest views: (a) an axial view showing a 4 cm focal consolidative lesion in the medial right upper lobe with a large central area of necrosis and early cavitation, and (b) a coronal view revealing the same necrotizing consolidation with cavitation extending from the right lung apex to the anterior right hilar region. The lesion appears well-demarcated with evidence of tissue destruction and air-filled cavitation.
visible_findings: focal consolidation in the right upper lobe
extension of cavitation from apex to hilar region

Case_19009/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3 a and b: Sagittal and coronal CT chest 1 month post completion of treatment revealed residual thin-walled cystic space

description.short_caption: Sagittal and coronal CT chest showing residual thin-walled cystic space post-treatment.
description.detailed_description: This image consists of two CT chest views: axial (A) and coronal (B). Both images reveal a residual thin-walled cystic space in the lung parenchyma, likely representing a sequela of prior infection or treatment. The lung fields show no significant consolidation or active infiltrates. The mediastinum and surrounding structures appear unremarkable. The images are post-treatment, as indicated by the absence of acute findings.
visible_findings: thin-walled cystic space in lung parenchyma
